decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm approach to the straightedge, rotating the gripper downward while keeping clearance; right arm stays home.
Continue the elevated left approach and downward orientation, without touching the blocks.
Finish the top-down approach above the left portion of the straightedge.
Rotate the left jaws across the straightedge's narrow width before descending; maintain the current elbow-up branch.
Move above the left-side grasp point and continue aligning the jaw opening across the tool. Right gripper remains open at home.
Complete jaw alignment at the current height. The tool shifted slightly during approach, so avoid further translation before checking contact.
Fine-position the open jaws over the displaced left end of the tool, descending conservatively while watching the contact geometry.
Close around the tool at the current tabletop contact height. Retention will be judged from subsequent tool motion, not the gripper command.
The tool does not appear centered in the closed jaws. Reopen, slightly relieve tabletop pressure, and advance to center the tool before regrasping.
Close at the revised grasp point, then make a short table-parallel motion to check whether the straightedge follows.
Relieve contact and open the left gripper above the straightedge so the jaws can be centered without continuing to pivot the tool.
Translate the raised open jaws forward to center over the visible left portion of the straightedge, keeping clear of all cubes.
Lower the now-centered jaws onto the straightedge and close, avoiding any cube contact or lift.
Allow the tool grasp to close, then gently square the long pushing edge toward a horizontal row while keeping it on the table.
Test a short, low straightedge advance with the gripper closed; check both ends of the tool for stable retention.
The free end is pivoting rather than translating. Hold the left contact and bring the right arm toward the right end to stabilize the straightedge, without crossing arms.
Continue the right-arm approach above the free end, with extra height to clear the tool during wrist rotation. Left contact stays fixed.
Finish the right top-down orientation above the right end, preserving clearance and elbow-up continuity.
Rotate the right jaws across the tool and move inward only within the right workspace; retain overhead clearance.
Continue aligning the right jaws while advancing over the right-hand grasp location; left hand holds its position.
Complete the right jaw orientation and center above the free end before lowering to stabilize it.
Lower the right jaws around the free end at the same working height as the left and close for two-point straightedge control.
Finish closing the right grasp and cautiously advance its end to reduce the straightedge's skew, while keeping both tool contacts low.
Advance the right end to straighten the pushing edge. Both hands stay at tabletop working height so the cubes slide rather than lift.
Improve low tool engagement with a small descent while continuing to square the right end. Avoid lifting any block.
The right end did not follow the last motion. Reopen and recenter slightly inward and back over the tool before re-engaging; keep the left contact fixed.
Raise the open right jaws clear of the straightedge before repositioning; the current contact is pushing its end rather than securing it.
Reposition the raised right gripper rearward until its jaws are over the straightedge rather than ahead of it; no block contact.
Descend with the right jaws open around the visually centered straightedge, stopping near tabletop height before closing.
Close the right gripper around the centered tool at low height and allow the contact to settle before pushing.
Use the lower right contact to advance the tool's right end and reduce its skew, while the left contact anchors the other end.
Continue advancing the retained right end to bring the straightedge toward a level row. Keep both grippers closed and the blocks sliding on the tabletop.
Finish bringing the right end level with the left, using the straightedge to square the near faces of the cubes.
The three blocks now appear in a straight parallel row. Withdraw the straightedge slightly without lifting, then release it before resetting both arms.
Lift only the released, open grippers clear of the straightedge. The cubes remain visibly aligned and untouched during the reset.
Begin the reset by retreating both open hands in their own workspaces and unwinding their yaw rotations, clear of the aligned cubes.
Continue the clear retreat and yaw reset, maintaining each arm's elbow-up configuration and leaving the aligned row undisturbed.
Finish unwinding both wrists to a common downward orientation during the clear rearward retreat, preparing to return to the original arm poses.
Rotate both wrists back toward their original forward orientation while retreating toward home on the same elbow-up branches.
Continue returning both arms toward their initial positions and orientations with small continuous increments; the cubes remain aligned.
